note: Every sentence that claims something does not exist, or that a provider prints a price it may not print, is signed off here. claim_check.py fails the deploy when a page still carries an entry marked refuted, and when an absence sentence has no entry at all. Quotes below are the providers' own wording, read on the date shown; no third-party page is used as evidence.

claims.claim: VPS has no first-term-to-renewal price jump to model.
claims.evidence: Refuted by the page's own table and by both providers' plan cards. ScalaHosting Build #1: $22.46/mo, "$54.95/mo when you renew" = 2.45x. Namecheap Spark: $3.88/mo, "Was $4.88/mo", "You pay $46.56 - renews at $58.56/year" = 1.26x. The sentence was removed on 2026-10-31.

claims.claim: OVHcloud prints a yearly sticker price equal to 12x its monthly.
claims.evidence: OVHcloud's VPS page prints one figure, "From $4.54 /month", with no yearly total and no renewal price; the configurator link behind the card carries pricing=upfront12, so $4.54 is already a 12-month-prepaid monthly equivalent. $54.48 a year is our own 12x, not a sticker. The sentence was removed on 2026-10-31.

claims.claim: None of the three providers publishes a bandwidth overage rate.
claims.evidence: DigitalOcean's Droplet table stops at 1,000 GiB outbound and quotes no price beyond it; OVHcloud states unlimited traffic; ScalaHosting states unmetered. No overage rate is printed on any of the three, so the line stays as 'Cannot be computed' rather than an estimate.

claims.claim: hosting.com (formerly A2 Hosting) publishes no public discount code.
claims.evidence: hosting.com's plan page prints the discounted first-term price directly and applies the promo identifier WH1YAL at checkout; no alphanumeric code field appears on the order flow, and the A2-era codes are not part of hosting.com's checkout. Verified against the plan page on 2026-10-13.

claims.claim: OVHcloud's VPS page prints no renewal price.
claims.evidence: The page prints one figure per plan, "From $4.54 /month", with no renewal line, no yearly total and no term table. The configurator link behind the card carries pricing=upfront12, which is the only statement about the term on the page.

claims.claim: DigitalOcean sells no billing term, so there is no renewal price to jump to.
claims.evidence: DigitalOcean prices Droplets per second with a 60-second or $0.01 minimum and a monthly cap; the price table offers no 12-month or 24-month commitment, so there is no first-term price and no renewal price.
